rubrics.criterion: Every responsibility area named in the task's scope — credential admission, request parsing and normalization, request and subtree authorization, per-user pipeline preparation, the OPTIONS and partial-update protocol stages, request logging and remote-IP resolution, and directory-listing filtering — is implemented by its own single-purpose unit (a type or a tight group of functions), and the request-handling entry point routes a request through those units rather than implementing each stage itself.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's central ask: the request pipeline stages were all gathered onto one owner, so the repair is judged on whether the distinct responsibilities were identified and re-homed as cohesive units, with the entry point left as orchestration. The repository's scope areas are concrete enough that a judge can verify each has a home, while the unit boundaries and names stay free.

rubrics.criterion: Per-request and per-subtree permission decisions are made by asking the rules/permission model to resolve — the call site provides the request and the predicate it needs, and the model's own resolution mechanism (its rule walk, including collection rules and the global permissions) decides — rather than the call site re-implementing the rule walk or re-shaping the model's data to make the decision itself.
rubrics.rationale: The injection duplicated the model's resolution role at the pipeline call site instead of composing it; restoring the ask-the-model seam is specific to this instance's permission architecture, not a generic quality vote.

rubrics.criterion: Request parsing and normalization have one cohesive home: the internal request record, the prefix stripping, the dot-segment resolution and the collection-versus-resource classification are owned by that home, downstream consumers receive the produced values rather than recomputing them, and the change does not leave a second copy of the normalization applied at consumer call sites.
rubrics.rationale: Parsing is the pipeline's most shared product — authorization and the underlying file system must see the same names — so whether it lives in one place with consumers receiving values is decidable from the patch and is specific to this codebase's path-agreement requirement.

rubrics.criterion: The per-user serving arrangement survives the reorganization: each configured user still has a per-user pipeline prepared at construction time (backing file system, lock namespace shaped like the user's mounts, and backing WebDAV handler), and an admitted request is still dispatched to that user's backing WebDAV handler after the pipeline's checks pass.
rubrics.rationale: The refactor moves request-time stage procedures, and the correctness of that move in this server depends on the construction-time per-user state and final dispatch staying intact — this is the coupled consequence of the extraction in this specific architecture.

rubrics.criterion: The filtered listing wrapper enforces read rules on its own terms: it derives the names it filters by the same normalization the library already uses for requests, without receiving name shaping — or any other behavior — from request-handling code as an injected function field or callback.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the listing wrapper was rewired to depend on the request-handling owner via a callback; re-established self-consistency between rules and listings is the tied-together consequence of moving parsing and authorization out, and is checkable against both the prompt and the patch.

rubrics.criterion: The partial-update protocol's pure policy helpers — update-range and Content-Range parsing, content-type validation, the WebDAV If-header parser, entity-tag matching and bounded body spooling — travel with, or remain reachable from, the protocol's serving unit instead of being orphaned or duplicated by the extraction.
rubrics.rationale: The serving stages and their byte-level policy were split apart by the injection; the sound repairs in this codebase keep them together (or reachable), which the judge can verify from the patch and the responsibility inventory.

rubrics.criterion: The normalization function field injected on the listing wrapper type is fully removed: no function-valued field, parameter or constructor argument threads a name-shaping callback from request-handling code into the wrapper remains.
rubrics.rationale: This callback threading is an obsolete injected artifact of the reorganization: leaving it in place keeps a phantom dependency between the listing layer and the request-handling owner even after the stages were extracted, and a judge can decide its presence from the patch alone.

rubrics.criterion: The extraction left the request handler type still declaring procedures it previously owned: unused or forwarding copies of pipeline stages such as per-user preparation, authentication, request parsing, request or subtree authorization, lock admission, partial-update preconditions or serving, OPTIONS serving, or request logging and remote-IP resolution remain on it as dead code beside the units that took the logic over.
rubrics.rationale: A common shortcut when re-homing logic is to add the new homes while never deleting the old ones, which leaves dead request pipeline stages inside the coordinator; this failure mode is specific to how the stages were gathered in this instance and is decidable from the patch.

rubrics.criterion: The reorganization strands no helper: every package-level function or type that the moved pipeline stages used — including the partial-update policy helpers, the rules model's resolution entry points, and the request parsing helpers — still has callers after the change.
rubrics.rationale: Extraction cuts call paths; in this instance the helpers are package-private, so a stranded one passes compilation silently, and its presence is visible in the final repository state the judge reviews.

rubrics.criterion: The exported construction surface the command wiring uses remains source-compatible: the same constructor call with the same configuration builds a working server, and the patch touches nothing in the command package.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's compatibility boundary is explicit in the task: the served API used by the command wiring must not move; a judge can confirm both the unchanged call surface and the untouched command package from the patch.

rubrics.criterion: The patch modifies, deletes or rewrites any test file, or otherwise weakens existing expectations — for example narrowing an assertion, removing a case, or making one conditional on an environment or configuration detail it did not previously depend on.
rubrics.rationale: The instance's behavioral safety net is the webdav test suite; a solver could make changed behavior pass by reshaping the tests instead of preserving behavior, which is exactly the shortcut this rubric exists to fail.

rubrics.criterion: Request logging remains wired through construction into the served requests: per-request log lines still carry the same fields (method, path, error, and remote address, as produced by the shared per-request logger), and the client address still resolves through the proxy header only behind the serving flag.
rubrics.rationale: Logging and proxy-aware address resolution were part of the moved stages in this instance, are only partially pinned by the test suite, and are observable in the repository after the change — so they need their own regression check.
